newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods prices steady to higher late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods prices steady to higher late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale product prices were steady to higher Thursday, brokers said, amid quiet afternoon trade, as distillates felt the aftershock of Tuesday's fire at the Tosco refinery near San Francisco.
Refinery and state labor officials on Wednesday began to investigate the fire's cause, which remained unknown today, the said.

A 1.01 million barrel build in West Coast gasoline stocks, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API), bearish under normal circumstance, was offset by the perceived supply tightness after the Tuesday plant fire, brokers said.
"Gasoline is flat and diesel is taking off," a broker said, noting that upcoming maintenance at Bay area Exxon, Unocal and Shell hydrocracking units would further stir supply concerns.
Offers for CARB grade gasoline in San Francisco were talked about a cent lower than Wednesday at 79.50 cents a gallon, while conventional grade was rumored flat.
CARB for all February deliveries was seen notionally unchanged from yesterday at 81.50 cents.
Meanwhile, jet fuel stayed 83/85 cents a gallon late after rising two cents early, amid supply concerns raised by the lost hydrocracker at Tosco.
